editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the NCLEX-RN nursing license exam certified by NCSBN, covering management of care, safety, pharmacology, and physiological adaptation.
editorial.overview: The NCLEX-RN (National Council Licensure Examination for Registered Nurses) is certified by NCSBN and evaluates nursing candidates across eight distinct domains, including management of care, safety and infection prevention, pharmacological therapies, and physiological adaptation, to help ensure safe and effective entry-level nursing practice for all candidates taking the examination.
editorial.who_should_take: Candidates seeking licensure as a registered nurse who have completed an approved nursing education program should take this examination to demonstrate entry-level clinical competence and safety.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official test plan and study all eight content domains. Focus heavily on high-weight areas such as management of care and pharmacological therapies. Practice answering clinical scenario questions and check with NCSBN for the current certification path to ensure adequate preparation for the 300-minute duration.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses on professional management of care principles, accounting for 18.0 percent of the total exam content to ensure that candidates understand effective nursing leadership, delegation, and care coordination.

This category covers safety and infection prevention and control measures, representing 13.0 percent of the exam content to ensure candidates can maintain secure healthcare environments and properly protect patients from potential hazards.

This domain addresses health promotion and maintenance strategies, making up 9.0 percent of the test plan to evaluate how nurses educate individuals on wellness, preventive health practices, and developmental stages across the lifespan.

This section encompasses psychosocial integrity concepts, contributing 9.0 percent to the overall weight by testing the nurse's ability to provide emotional support, manage mental health challenges, and address therapeutic communication needs effectively.

This area pertains to basic care and comfort, spanning 9.0 percent of the examination to ensure that registered nurses can competently assist patients with activities of daily living, personal hygiene, and proper nutritional support.
study_focus: Assistance with activities of daily living

domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses on pharmacological and parenteral therapies, accounting for 16.0 percent of the exam to evaluate medication administration safety, dosage calculations, and the continuous monitoring of intravenous and complex drug regimens.

This category covers the reduction of risk potential, representing 12.0 percent of the test content by measuring the nurse's capacity to anticipate diagnostic test outcomes, recognize potential complications, and implement preventative clinical interventions.

This final domain addresses physiological adaptation, making up 14.0 percent of the total exam weight to assess how nurses manage severe alterations in body systems, unexpected clinical deterioration, and acute medical emergencies.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at the testing center prepared for a 300-minute examination. Manage your time carefully across the 8 domains and read each question carefully before selecting an answer.

faq.question_title: How many domains are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam is divided into 8 distinct domains, each carrying a specific weight percentage ranging from 9.0 percent to 18.0 percent of the total test plan.
The passing score for this examination is established at or above the official passing standard determined by the governing board of the NCSBN to ensure nursing competency.
Candidates taking this professional nursing examination are allotted a total duration of exactly 300 minutes to complete all test questions presented during the testing session without exceptions.
The examination is officially certified and administered under the regulatory authority of the NCSBN for all nursing candidates seeking professional licensure in the modern healthcare field today.

methodology.summary: This index page was structured using the official exam guide published by NCSBN, detailing the 8 content domains, passing standards, and duration.
